LESSON: SWADAQAH (CHARITY)

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.3: Swadaqah (Charity)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swadaqah (Charity), part of Devotional Acts in Grade 5 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What acts of swadaqah do Muslims perform? 2.What are the benefits of practising swadaqah?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify forms of swadaqah for character development,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swadaqah (Charity) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. demonstrate different acts of swadaqah to earn rewards,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swadaqah (Charity) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. assess the benefits of practising acts of swadaqah in society,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swadaqah (Charity) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the different forms of swadaqah in their daily life.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Swadaqah (Charity) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify forms of swadaqah for character development,

   Swadaqah (Charity) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. demonstrate different acts of swadaqah to earn rewards,

   Swadaqah (Charity) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. assess the benefits of practising acts of swadaqah in society,

   Swadaqah (Charity) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. appreciate the different forms of swadaqah in their daily life.

   Swadaqah (Charity) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class,

2. discuss the different forms of swadaqah, in pairs/groups, as per the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w) (such as feeding an animal, removing an obstacle/harmful from the path/roads, sharing with others),

3. participate in charitable activities (clean-up exercise, visit to children’s home, tree planting),

4. discuss the benefits of giving charity and make class presentation. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class,
2. discuss the different forms of swadaqah, in pairs/groups, as per the teachings of the Prophet (s.a.w) (such as feeding an animal, removing an obstacle/harmful from the path/roads, sharing with others),
3. participate in charitable activities (clean-up exercise, visit to children’s home, tree planting),
4. discuss the benefits of giving charity and make class presentation. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swadaqah (Charity) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the skills of listening, speaking and teamwork enhanced as learners discuss the benefits

of giving charity and making class presentation.

• Leaning to learn: the skill of working collaboratively as learners participate in charitable activities (clean-up exercise, visit to

children’s home, tree planting).

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as learners get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in

class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Empathy as learners participate in charitable activities (clean up exercise, visit to children’s home, tree planting)

Links to other Learning Areas:
Creative Arts as learners get pictures from digital devices/print media on forms of swadaqah and display them in class.
